sentences.text: Since these appeals arise out of the same accident they have been heard together and are being decided by a common order.

02. These appeals under Section 173 (1) of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 have been preferred by the appellants/claimants Rubeena Bee and Nikku @ Nikhar being aggrieved by the award dated 13.08.2024 passed in MACC No.159/2023 and MACC No.160/2023 by the Additional Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal, Badnagar, District Ujjain whereby compensation has been awarded to them.

entities.text: Additional Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal, Badnagar
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:6105 2 MA-9319-2024 03.
As per the appellants, on 10.07.2022, they were going on a motorcycle from Badnagar to Gram Samar.

When they reached Bangred Petrol Pump, respondent No.1 drove vehicle bearing registration No.MP-09- WD-2076 of which he was the owner and which was insured with Nikku @ Nikhar vs Suryajeet on 7 March, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/125433179/
1 respondent No.2
in a rash and negligent manner and dashed the same against their motorcycle as a result of which they fell down and suffered grievous injuries.
They were taken to the hospital for treatment where they remained under treatment for a considerable period of time.

04. Thereafter, the appellants filed separate claim applications under Section 166 of the Act, 1988 before the Claims Tribunal for award of compensation to them on account of the accident suffered by them.
The applications were contested by the non-applicants by filing their written statements to the same.
Upon evaluation of the evidence brought on record by the parties the Claims Tribunal has awarded compensation to the appellants as aforesaid.
05. These appeals for enhancement of amount of compensation have been preferred by the appellants on the ground that in the accident they had suffered grievous injuries.
They had been taken to the hospital for treatment where they underwent treatment for a long period of time.
Due to the accident, they had suffered a considerable amount of pain and had to undergo extreme hardships.
Their family members also had to be involved in their treatment at all time.
Due to the accident, the appellants were unable to perform any work.
The amount which has been awarded by the Claims Tribunal under various heads is quite inadequate.
It is hence submitted that NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:6105 3 MA-9319-2024 the amount awarded to the appellants by way of compensation be enhanced appropriately.

06. Per contra, learned counsel for respondent No.2, Insurance Company has submitted that just and fair amount of compensation has been awarded to the appellants in which no interference is warranted in view of which the appeals deserve to be dismissed.
07. I have considered the submissions of the learned counsel for the parties and have perused the record.
08. The record indicates that in the accident the appellants had suffered grievous injuries on various parts of their body.
They had been taken to the hospital for treatment.
They underwent treatment at the hospital for a considerable period of time.
In the accident, they had suffered extreme pain and also fracture on their body.
They had to incur heavy expenditure on their treatment and had to keep attendant with them and to take special diet.
Due to the accident, they were unable to perform their regular work.

Considering the nature of the accident, the injuries suffered by the appellants and in the available facts and circumstances of the case, in my opinion, the amount awarded by the Claims Tribunal to the appellants is inadequate.
09. It is hence held that the appellant Nikku @ Nikhar in M.A. No.9320/2024 shall be entitled for enhanced lump-sum amount of compensation in the sum of Rs.8,500/-.
The appellant Rubeena Bee in M.A. No.9319/2024 shall be entitled for enhanced lump-sum amount of compensation in the sum of Rs.48,000/-.

The aforesaid enhanced amount of compensation shall be payable to the appellants along with interest at the rate NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:6105 4 MA-9319-2024 of 6% per annum from the date of filing of the claim applications by them till date of payment.
10. The appeals are accordingly partly allowed and disposed off.
